terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js starts your API on a free port and sends it a few requests.

tasks.title: Read one workshop by id
tasks.description:
Add a route to `createApp` in `src/app.js`:

- `GET /workshops/:id` answers `200` with the workshop whose id is `:id`, as `store.get(id)` returns it
- an id the store does not have, or one that is not a number at all (`/workshops/glazing`), answers `404` with `{ "error": { "code": "not_found", "message": "..." } }`

Ids in the store are numbers. The check sends ids of workshops it gave the store, ids it did not, and one that is not a number.
nextSteps: Add a route whose path has a parameter for the id.
Read the id from the request and turn it into a number.
Ask the store for that workshop.
Answer 404 when there is none, then run `node try.js`.
hints: A part of a path that starts with `:` is a route parameter. Express puts what the client sent there in `req.params`.
Everything in `req.params` is text, and the store's ids are numbers. `'3' === 3` is false.
`store.get(Number(req.params.id))` gives a workshop or `undefined`. Return a `res.status(404).json(...)` when it is `undefined`.

tasks.title: Filter the list by day
tasks.description:
Make `GET /workshops` take an optional filter in the query string:

- `GET /workshops?day=thu` answers only the workshops whose `day` is `thu`, in the store's order
- a day with no workshops answers `200` with an empty list
- without `day`, the list is whole, as before

The check asks for days that have workshops, a day that has none, and no day at all.
nextSteps: Read the query string from the request in the list route.
Keep the whole list when there is no `day`.
Otherwise keep only the workshops on that day.
Run `node try.js` and look at the `?day=thu` answer.
hints: Express has already split the query string into an object for you. Look at `req.query`.
A filter that was not sent is `undefined` in `req.query`. Only filter when it is there.

tasks.title: Filter it by price
tasks.description:
Add a second optional filter to `GET /workshops`:

- `?maxPriceCents=4000` keeps only the workshops whose `priceCents` is at most that number
- with `day` and `maxPriceCents` both given, keep the workshops that match both
- a `maxPriceCents` that is not a number answers `400` with `{ "error": { "code": "bad_query", "message": "..." } }`

The check sends prices on and around the edge, both filters together, and a price that is not a number.
nextSteps: Turn it into a number, and decide what to do when that fails.
Keep only what costs that much or less, after the day filter.
Run `node try.js` and look at the last two answers.
hints: Query values are always text, like route parameters. Comparing a price with `'4000'` happens to work, but `'cheap'` becomes `NaN`, and every comparison with `NaN` is false.
`Number('cheap')` is `NaN`, and `Number.isNaN` tells you so. That is the moment to answer 400 and stop.
Convert once, return `res.status(400).json(...)` when `Number.isNaN(max)`, then chain a second `.filter` that keeps `w.priceCents <= max`.
